subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For interrupted long Codex-backed maintenance turns, should OpenClaw automatically resume after Gateway restart, synthesize a status/failure follow-up, or fail closed with explicit no-replay guidance?
rationale: The code can detect parts of the failure, but the correct behavior depends on maintainer policy for replaying side-effecting maintenance work and for distinguishing intentional shutdown from unexpected app-server loss across channels.

options.title: Resume only when safe
options.body: Resume from the existing transcript only when Codex/session metadata says replay or continuation is safe, and otherwise deliver a clear unresumable interruption notice.

options.title: Always send status only
options.body: Do not resume maintenance turns automatically; instead send a post-restart interrupted-status notice with guidance for the user to request a fresh status check.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Keep the current retry/recovery behavior while collecting a live current-main reproduction that narrows the app-server close trigger before choosing product behavior.

recommendation.title: Resume only when safe
recommendation.body: Resume from the existing transcript only when Codex/session metadata says replay or continuation is safe, and otherwise deliver a clear unresumable interruption notice.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Codex app-server lifecycle, Gateway restart behavior, channel delivery, and replay-safety policy, and steipete has the strongest mixed history signal across those boundaries.
